s.en: show / manipulate the IP routing table
s.es: muestra o cambia la tabla de rutas (antigua; hoy se usa ip route)

syn: route [-CFvnNee] [-A family |-4|-6] ⏎ route [-v] [-A family |-4|-6] add [-net|-host] target [netmask Nm] [gw Gw] [metric N] [mss M] [window W] [irtt I] [reject] [mod] [dyn] [reinstate] [[dev] If] ⏎ route [-v] [-A family |-4|-6] del [-net|-host] target [gw Gw] [netmask Nm] [metric M] [[dev] If] ⏎ route [-V] [--version] [-h] [--help]

o.en: Show numerical addresses instead of trying to determine symbolic host names.
use the specified address family (eg `inet'). Use route --help for a full list. You can use -6 as an alias for --inet6 and -4 as an alias for -A inet
operate on the kernel's FIB (Forwarding Information Base) routing table. This is the default.
operate on the kernel's routing cache.
use netstat(8)-format for displaying the routing table. -ee will generate a very long line with all parameters from the routing table.
